command:
/audit

Illustrative sample only. No research or AI request was performed.
limitations: This is a fictional illustration, not a live audit.
No external pages, competitors, trends or analytics were checked.
Sample calendar copy illustrates fields and is deliberately reusable; a configured live audit generates brand-specific copy.

report.summary: An illustrative hospitality design studio with a clear niche and an opportunity to make its enquiry process easier to understand. This sample demonstrates the report structure; it is not a real audit.
unknowns: No website or social content was inspected.
Buyer needs, offers, competitors and results are not verified.
questions: Who is the primary buyer and target market?
Which offer, proof and enquiry destination are approved?
What is the production capacity and approval process?

findings.title: A specific audience
findings.assessment: Illustrative observation: the fictional studio focuses on independent hospitality businesses.
findings.recommendation: Check that the real homepage makes its audience equally clear.

findings.title: An unclear enquiry process
findings.assessment: Illustrative gap: the sample does not explain what happens after an enquiry.
findings.recommendation: Explain the first step and set accurate expectations.

findings.title: Commercial performance
findings.assessment: There are no analytics or sales records in this example.
findings.recommendation: Establish a qualified-enquiry baseline before judging results.

modules.title: Executive brand summary
modules.observations: Fictional example: Fieldwork Studio designs practical brand identities for independent hospitality businesses.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Proposed profile: B2B design studio; audience: hospitality founders; geography: Needs Client Confirmation; offer: Needs Client Confirmation; voice: practical, calm and precise; approval owner: Needs Client Confirmation.

modules.title: Sources reviewed and research limitations
modules.observations: This is an illustrative report. No live website, social profile or customer data was accessed.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Use Sources & limits to distinguish inspected evidence, client context and assumptions. A real audit lists each supplied link and its access result.

modules.title: Website audit
modules.observations: The fictional homepage identifies a specialism, but the sample copy does not explain the enquiry process.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Proposed homepage structure: who we help → relevant work → process → project-fit criteria → one clear enquiry CTA. Verify that each section fits the actual offer.

modules.title: Social media audit
modules.observations: No social profile was inspected. Visual consistency and posting frequency cannot be assessed.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Before evaluating performance, supply accessible recent posts or an anonymised export with dates, URLs and formats. Private reach and conversions need analytics.

modules.title: Marketing funnel audit
modules.observations: The proposed journey is discovery → portfolio → project enquiry → qualification call. No conversion results are available.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Awareness: useful opening-day questions. Nurture: explain design trade-offs. Positioning: verified process examples. Lead generation: project-fit enquiry. Conversion: answer scope and next-step questions.

modules.title: SWOT analysis
modules.observations: Illustrative strength: a clear hospitality specialism. Potential weakness: an unexplained first step. Opportunity hypothesis: educate founders about opening-day brand decisions. Threat hypothesis: price-based comparison.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Test the opportunity hypothesis with five actual founder conversations. Confirm whether uncertainty about design scope is a meaningful barrier before prioritising it.

modules.title: Competitor analysis
modules.observations: No real competitors were researched for this sample.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: A live report aims to compare 3–5 relevant alternatives using public positioning, offers, proof, content and CTAs. Missing competitors stay unverified.

modules.title: Buyer persona and psychology map
modules.observations: Buyer hypothesis: an independent café founder preparing an opening. Needs Client Confirmation: budget, decision process and actual customer language.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: PAIN: too many launch decisions. IDENTITY: an independent operator. DESIRE: a coherent customer experience. FEAR: expensive rework. VILLAIN: fragmented advice. FRUSTRATION: generic templates. RISK: unclear scope. OBJECTION: timing and cost. All eight are hypotheses pending customer evidence.

modules.title: Brand positioning recommendations
modules.observations: A potential position is practical brand design for independent hospitality founders. This is a proposal, not an approved promise.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Proposed value statement: Brand decisions that work across the places your customers meet you. Use plain explanations. Avoid unverified revenue promises, guaranteed launch results and invented testimonials.

modules.title: Trend intelligence and opportunity ranking
modules.observations: No current trend claims are made. No live research was performed.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Research market-relevant industry changes and audience questions, then confirm dates and relevance. Only evidence-backed candidates receive the weighted 100-point score. Safety overrides that score.

modules.title: Recommended marketing strategy
modules.observations: Proposed objective: attract suitable brand-design enquiries by explaining the process and showing verified work.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Prioritise clear offers, a credible process and relevant examples. Start with a manageable production cadence. Test education and objection-handling before scaling volume.

modules.title: Content pillars and funnel plan
modules.observations: Four proposed pillars: opening-day decisions, design explained, the working process, and project-fit questions.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Opening-day decisions: awareness; founder checklist; saves. Design explained: nurture; visual example; qualified questions. Working process: positioning; real process walkthrough; portfolio visits. Project-fit questions: conversion; scope explainer; suitable enquiries. Verify all proof and assets.

modules.title: Platform-specific recommendations
modules.observations: Instagram could show visual reasoning; LinkedIn could explain the business decisions behind the work. Audience preference is unverified.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Instagram: annotated visual sequences with clear captions. LinkedIn: a focused decision, evidence and business implication. Adapt each format rather than reposting unchanged. Confirm the target audience uses each channel.

modules.title: Lead generation and conversion improvements
modules.observations: The enquiry form and qualification process were not tested.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Discovery → profile visit → useful example → enquiry → follow-up → qualification → project decision → referral. Proposed owner: studio lead. Verify destination, consent language, response expectations and qualification criteria.

modules.title: First 30-day content calendar
modules.observations: The Content studio shows 30 illustrative daily draft entries. This example is not a verified client calendar.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: One draft per day is illustrative. Client capacity, campaign dates and approved offers must determine the final publishing frequency. Every entry remains DRAFT — NEEDS APPROVAL.

modules.title: KPI framework
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Awareness: relevant profile visits. Nurture: useful questions and saves when available. Lead generation: qualified enquiries. Conversion: suitable enquiries progressing to a call. Establish baselines and compare controlled tests; do not infer causation from engagement.

modules.title: Priority action plan
modules.observations: Address unclear enquiry expectations before increasing traffic.
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: 1. Clarify who the offer fits. 2. Explain the first enquiry step. 3. Gather approved project proof. 4. Test two educational angles. 5. Measure qualified enquiries.

modules.title: Client confirmation questions
plan: Confirm the facts and assumptions below with the client.
Use the proposed deliverable as a discussion draft.
modules.deliverable: Which services and locations are approved? What makes a good-fit enquiry? Which work can be shown? Who approves content? How much content can the team produce?

actions.title: Clarify the first step
steps: Draft a short explanation of who responds and what happens next.
Review the wording with the client before any live change.
actions.kpi: Qualified enquiries and completed enquiries, once measurable

actions.title: Gather credible project proof
actions.why: Support positioning with evidence rather than broad claims.
steps: Identify a real project cleared for publication.
Record the problem, design decisions and supported outcome.
Check client permission for assets and claims.
actions.kpi: Relevant portfolio visits and enquiry quality
actions.dependency: Approved assets and factual project details
